content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} sales tax on a vehicle, one rate for the whole state, plus a title fee and a registration fee that depends on the vehicle's weight and model year.

howItWorks.text: The sales tax rate is {stateRate} everywhere in the state. A trade-in shown on the dealer's invoice is taken off the price before the tax is figured.
Registration is charged by weight class, and the fee is higher for a vehicle from a recent model year. A new passenger vehicle pays for four years at once.
New vehicles that cost a lot or use a lot of fuel carry an extra surcharge that the dealer collects. Zero emission vehicles pay a yearly fee that rises over time.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in New Jersey?
faq.text: Yes. When the dealer's invoice shows a trade-in, its price is subtracted from the price of the vehicle before sales tax.

faq.q: Is there a local sales tax in New Jersey?
faq.text: No. The state has a single sales tax rate for the entire state.
Dealers collect an extra surcharge on a new vehicle that costs a set amount or more, or that gets poor fuel economy.

faq.q: Why does registration cost more up front on a new vehicle?
faq.text: New passenger vehicles pay for four years of registration at once.
